title: Alumni-discount claim matched to a transit or telecom subscriber account
moment: A graduate renews a subsidised or alumni-linked service (for example a campus-partner telecom plan, a university-affiliated co-working or gym membership, or an alumni association rate) and the vendor wants proof that the person holding the subscription account is the same person the university recognises as an alumnus.
verifier: Alumni association or partner vendor offering alumni pricing
predicate: The person who holds a university-signed alumnus credential is the same person as the holder of a second issuer's credential (a telecom or membership account credential), proven without revealing the national ID or student number to the vendor.
disclosed_today: Photo of national ID, student or alumni card, graduation year, department, phone number, sometimes a scanned diploma.
issuer: University (alumnus status claim), matched to a telecom or membership issuer's subscriber claim
why_zk: The vendor needs only one bit, that this account holder is an alumnus, but today it collects the ID, department and graduation year, which are all unneeded. The match is the hard part, since both credentials must bind to the same person without a shared identifier. Weakness is that few vendors and no telecom issuer currently issue verifiable credentials, so the second issuer side is hypothetical, and the stakes are small enough that a staff glance at an alumni card is the cheaper practice.

title: Proving a tenant's subsidised-utility status to a landlord or social-housing agency without revealing the rented address
moment: A person applying for a rent subsidy or a social-housing waitlist slot must show they currently hold a utility account on the subsidised roll, but the agency is also a different locality from the one they rent in, and the applicant does not want a prospective landlord or agency to see the address and usage history.
verifier: Municipal housing bureau or social-housing intermediary (e.g. a city social housing agency or a rent-subsidy application window)
predicate: The applicant's utility account belongs to the set of accounts on the subsidised-rate roll (and is active), without revealing which account or address.
disclosed_today: Recent utility bills with address and consumption, lease copy, household registration, and sometimes several months of statements to show continuity.
why_zk: The agency wants to know the person is a bona fide low-income occupant, but collects address, usage and the lease, which also lets staff and intermediaries profile occupancy. Honest caveat: rent-subsidy eligibility is defined by income and asset tests via the tax and household registration data, so a utility subsidy roll is only a weak, partial signal and cannot replace those checks. It is most plausible as an extra anti-fraud tie-in (the address is a real, occupied dwelling), where some fields are legitimately required by the agency anyway.

title: Ride-hailing driver rating and trip count for a fleet-leasing deposit waiver
moment: A part-time driver in Taipei applies to a car-leasing or fleet company that waives the deposit for proven reliable drivers. Today the company asks for screenshots of the driver app showing earnings history, ratings, and trip details.
verifier: Fleet leasing company or taxi/ride-hailing fleet operator
predicate: Completed trips on the platform in the last 12 months >= 500 and average rating >= 4.8
disclosed_today: Full screenshots of the driver account, including passenger names or addresses in trip lists, daily earnings, platform account ID, and phone number
issuer: The ride-hailing platform account page, via a zkTLS session proof over the driver's logged-in API response (the platform does not issue credentials)
why_zk: The platform has no credential product, so only a TLS-session proof can attest the numbers; screenshots are trivially forged today. Weakness: the platform's terms may forbid automated access, and a proof only shows the page said so at that time, with no platform liability behind it. Trip count and rating are a narrow threshold, so the leasing company learns far less than from a full screenshot.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that a collector should not exceed the necessary scope of its purpose, applied to a deposit decision that needs only two thresholds rather than a full account view.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A rule requires anyone collecting personal data to stay within the necessary scope of its stated purpose, but it gives no concrete way to show what was necessary, so the collector decides what counts as necessary. | mechanism: Legal purpose-limitation and proportionality principle; no technical mechanism specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The failure of a verifier relying on easily copied artifacts, here screenshots, which a proof bound to the live session replaces.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A provider must verify that a new applicant is the named person, but its check uses identifiers that are easy to copy, so a stolen identity passes and the real person bears the consequences. | mechanism: None; online verification only checked ID number and issue date.

title: One vote per resident in a building or community management committee online poll
moment: An apartment community (a Taiwanese condominium management committee) runs an online vote on a repair levy or elevator replacement, and wants each household member or owner-resident counted once without a roll of who voted how.
verifier: The condominium management committee or its property management company.
predicate: The voter is one unique real subscriber and has not already cast a ballot in this poll (poll-scoped uniqueness), with no phone number or name revealed.
disclosed_today: Name, unit number, phone number, LINE ID, and often a photo of the national ID or the property deed sent through a group chat.
issuer: A telco that can sign the person as one real subscriber; ownership or residency would still need a separate attestation.
why_zk: Residents often fear neighbors learning how they voted on money disputes, and today the committee chair sees everyone's LINE and phone. A scoped uniqueness proof stops duplicate voting by one person with several numbers. Honest weakness: a telco credential proves only one person, not that the person lives in or owns a unit in this building, so this idea is weak unless combined with an owner or residency credential, and Taiwan's condominium law has its own rules on proxy and written ballots that may require named records.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The tension that a default of publishing who participated can flip to full exposure, with confidentiality only by exception, which motivated making ballot privacy the default.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: Someone must be drawn from a pool and seated for a task without the wider public learning who they are, but the default rule can flip to full publication of the identities of everyone selected, with confidentiality only as a judge-level exception. | mechanism: Judge-discretionary confidentiality of juror names under a court's jury selection plan; no technical mechanism specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The point that outsiders in the room break confidentiality, here the property manager and group-chat members who see everything.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party must consult an advisor about a sensitive matter without the advisor, or anyone else, learning or revealing more than the matter requires, but the protection breaks as soon as an outsider is in the room unless the outsider is essential to the relationship. | mechanism: Evidentiary privilege over communications, lost by third-party presence except essential agents such as interpreters; no technical mechanism.

title: Alumni-discount student-ID match at a Taiwan High Speed Rail or TRA concession counter
moment: A graduate student buys a student concession fare or a campus-partner ticket at a station counter or kiosk and is asked to show a student card plus national ID so the clerk can see both names match.
verifier: Railway or bus operator concession desk, or a third-party ticketing vendor handling campus partner deals
predicate: The enrolled-student claim signed by the university and the holder of the digital wallet national-ID credential refer to the same person, shown as a match proof without revealing the national ID number or student number.
disclosed_today: Student card (name, student number, photo, department, validity sticker) and often national ID card shown side by side or photographed for the sales record.
issuer: University (enrolment status) cross-matched with the national digital wallet identity credential.
why_zk: The verifier only needs "this current student is the person standing here", yet today it sees student number, department, ID number and birthdate. A match proof between the university claim and the wallet credential avoids that. Honest weakness is that concession fares are low value and clerks are used to a quick glance at the card, so adoption pressure is small, and the in-person photo check is arguably still needed.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that a counter should record only the fields a rule requires rather than keeping a full copy of the identity document.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A registrant must prove a small set of facts to a host, but the host asks for a full copy of the identity document, which carries many extra fields the rule never needed. | mechanism: Inspect the identity document in person and record only the fields the registration rule requires; no copy retained.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The proof should show a prior check passed without acting as a persistent identifier across repeated purchases.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A gatekeeper only needs to know that the visitor already passed some check, but the proof it accepts doubles as a persistent identifier. | mechanism: Blind-signed tokens that attest prior authorisation and cannot be linked to the issuance interaction.

title: Proving no outstanding exit restriction at the airport check-in counter
moment: A Taiwanese traveler checks in for an international flight, and the airline or ground handler must confirm the passenger is not subject to a government travel ban (出境限制, for example from tax arrears or court orders) before issuing a boarding pass, or a travel agent confirms it before booking a non-refundable group tour.
verifier: Airline ground-handling staff or a travel agency booking desk
predicate: The holder's national ID is not on the current exit-restriction register (non-membership), signed with a short validity window.
disclosed_today: Full passport and national ID number, often copied or photographed. If a restriction exists, staff can see it, and the traveler may be questioned about the reason in front of others.
issuer: National Immigration Agency, drawing on court and tax-authority restriction records
why_zk: A non-membership proof would let the verifier see only that the person is not restricted, so a clear traveler reveals nothing else. Weakness, stated honestly. Border control (immigration at departure) already checks the register itself and carriers have little legal duty to check, so this mostly removes a copy of the passport rather than a real check. A restricted person simply cannot produce the proof, and that failure itself tells the verifier something. The proof must be fresh, because a restriction can be imposed hours before departure.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: A check that relies only on copyable ID details is weak, which motivates a signed, fresh, holder-bound proof of the register status instead of a passport photocopy.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A provider must verify that a new applicant is the named person, but its check uses identifiers that are easy to copy, so a stolen identity passes and the real person bears the consequences. | mechanism: None; online verification only checked ID number and issue date.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that leakage should be bounded and checkable, applied by making the only thing the verifier learns a single yes bit about the register.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A releaser must answer queries about a dataset so that an observer learns almost nothing about whether any one individual contributed, and the leak must be expressed as a bound that can be checked. | mechanism: Differential privacy, a randomised release mechanism with a quantified privacy-loss parameter; NIST notes that the guarantee depends on how the framework is realised in practice and lists privacy hazards that can break it.

title: Overseas-study sponsor shows enough funds without handing a school the family's whole account history
moment: A Taiwanese family applying for a student visa or university admission abroad must show a parent's bank statements proving funds for tuition and living costs for the first year, and the parent sends months of statements to a foreign admissions office or visa agent.
verifier: Foreign university admissions office, embassy, or study-abroad agency in Taiwan
predicate: The sponsor's combined balance across the bank's accounts has stayed at or above the required amount (for example NT$1,000,000) for each of the last 90 days.
disclosed_today: Full statements and sometimes a copy of the national ID, revealing the family's spending, other relatives' transfers, employer, and exact balances well above the threshold.
issuer: The sponsor's bank, signing a minimum-balance-over-period aggregate across the sponsor's accounts at that bank.
why_zk: Only a threshold held over a period matters, and the exact balance and history stay hidden. A bank-signed aggregate also helps against doctored statements. Weakness: foreign institutions set their own formats and will rarely accept a Taiwan wallet proof, so uptake depends on the receiving side, and an agent in the middle often insists on seeing paper statements.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: A cross-border intermediary requiring full ID or document copies with no lighter alternative stated.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A foreign investor must prove that its local agent is a real, identified person, and the agent hands over a full copy of an ID card, with no alternative verification stated. | mechanism: None stated; full ID copy required with no less-intrusive alternative given.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: Bundles of identity and financial document copies requested when a narrower check could satisfy the purpose.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service provider signing up a customer must check identity and payment, but it asks for full front-and-back copies of identity and card documents, and the regulator leaves whether that exceeds the purpose to case-by-case fact-finding. | mechanism: None stated; the letter says less-intrusive alternatives must be considered but names none.

title: Seller reputation on an auction platform as a threshold for a high-value in-person handover
moment: A buyer of a used camera or console arranged on a second-hand marketplace is asked by a seller to prove being a trusted buyer before the seller will meet at a convenience store pickup point, or a seller is asked to prove good standing before a buyer pays by a third-party escrow.
verifier: The counterparty in a private sale, or a convenience-store pickup service gating a high-value parcel
predicate: Account positive-feedback share is at least 98 percent with at least 30 reviews, on an account older than one year
disclosed_today: The account name and link to the profile, which exposes the whole transaction history, other listings, location hints and sometimes real name; or the counterparty's phone number and LINE ID
issuer: Second-hand or auction marketplace account, with a zkTLS proof over the platform's profile or feedback API response
why_zk: A proof can show good standing while the buyer remains pseudonymous and without exposing other listings. Weak points: feedback on these platforms is already public by design, so the benefit is mainly unlinking the proof from the profile page and hiding the account name, and a proof of a good record does not stop an account being bought or rented out.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: Unlinkability, so the verifier cannot track the person across contexts.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A gatekeeper needs one yes/no fact about a holder, and the proof it receives must not reveal the underlying birth date or let the issuer or the gatekeeper track the holder. | mechanism: Zero-knowledge proof on ISO 18013-7 mdocs for an over-18 statement, device-bound transactions, no server-side storage of credential data.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: Disclosing one attribute out of a larger record the holder cannot split themselves.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A verifier needs one attribute from a larger identity record, but the holder cannot share just that attribute from the record. | mechanism: Selective disclosure of attributes from electronic attestations held in the EU Digital Identity Wallet.
